description:
Operational discipline surfaced 2026-05-05 by PRINCIPAL during the xft.7 quality cluster sequential gauntlet dispatches.

When user-tier POLYBIUS authors activation pastes for sequential engagements that all use the same role file (e.g., MAJOR_PLINY_<workspace> for multiple consecutive batches) AND the same cwd / project, the right pattern is to /clear the existing Claude Code session and re-paste the new engagement brief — not to instruct PRINCIPAL to open a fresh Claude Code session.

Why:
- Same shell environment preserved (cwd, env vars, terminal state)
- No respawn overhead (no Claude Code launch, no re-discovering MCP servers, no re-loading project CLAUDE.md autoloads)
- One terminal window for the whole sequential queue; less window-juggling for PRINCIPAL
- Mirrors the agent-infrastructure-stays-up-by-default principle (operating-disciplines.md §10/§11): tearing down infrastructure that costs nothing to keep is wrong; /clear is teardown-of-just-the-conversation-context, not teardown-of-the-session

When /clear is correct:
- Sequential dispatches against the same role file
- Continuing work in the same project / same cwd / same auth state
- Previous engagement closed cleanly

When fresh session is correct:
- Different role required
- Different cwd / different project
- Need to test cold-start activation flow itself
- Want parallel streams of work running

Where in substrate:
Likely operating-disciplines.md (universal-team layer) since this applies to any seat authoring activation pastes. Could also be a small note in MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md §5 (onboarding flow / activation patterns).

Recommendation: append a short subsection to operating-disciplines.md §8.1 (positive references) or as a new subsection §8.3 (activation paste patterns), since it's a discipline applied when authoring downstream-agent activation paste-instructions.

Empirical anchor: 2026-05-05 — Batch B activation paste (xft.7 quality cluster) was authored with 'open a fresh Claude Code session' framing when PRINCIPAL wanted /clear-then-repaste. Saved as user-tier feedback memory immediately; filing here so substrate inherits it on next install.
title: Activation pattern: /clear in existing session preferred over fresh-session for sequential dispatches against same role + cwd
